---
name: surf
description: Control Chrome through the surf CLI for browser testing, screenshots, form filling, page inspection, network and CPU emulation, DevTools data, and AI sites that use your logged-in Chrome session.
---

# Surf Browser Automation

`surf` gives agents a real Chrome session. Use it when shell-only checks cannot prove browser behavior: page state, clicks, forms, screenshots, console output, network requests, viewport changes, or AI sites that require your logged-in Chrome profile.

When command syntax is uncertain, ask the CLI first.

```bash
surf --help
surf <group>
surf --help-full
surf --find <term>
surf --help-topic <topic>
```

## First pass on a page

```bash
surf navigate "https://example.com"
surf page.read
surf page.read --compact
surf page.state
surf screenshot --output /tmp/shot.png
```

Read the page before clicking. Refs from `page.read` usually survive markup churn better than CSS selectors. Semantic locators work well when the intent is visible in the UI.

```bash
surf click --ref e1
surf locate.role button --name "Submit" --action click
surf locate.label "Email" --action fill --value "test@example.com"
surf locate.text "Accept" --exact --action click
```

## Browser targets

```bash
surf tab.list
surf tab.new "https://google.com"
surf tab.switch 12345
surf tab.name myapp
surf tab.switch myapp
surf tab.close 12345

surf window.list --tabs
surf window.new "https://example.com"
surf --window-id 123 page.read
surf window.focus 12345
surf window.resize --id 123 --width 1920 --height 1080
```

Use a separate window when agent work should not disturb your normal tabs.

## Read, act, wait

```bash
surf page.text
surf page.read --ref e5
surf element.styles e5
surf element.styles ".card"

surf click --x 100 --y 200
surf click --ref e5
surf type --text "hello"
surf type --text "hello" --selector "#input" --method js
surf key Enter
surf key "cmd+a"
surf hover --ref e5
surf drag --from-x 100 --from-y 100 --to-x 200 --to-y 200

surf scroll.bottom
surf scroll.to --ref e5
surf scroll.by --y 200
surf scroll.info

surf wait 2
surf wait.element ".loaded"
surf wait.network
surf wait.url "/success"
surf wait.dom --stable 100
surf wait.load
```

Use `--method js` when CDP typing fails in rich text editors.

## Forms and embedded contexts

```bash
surf form.fill --data '[{"ref":"e1","value":"John"},{"ref":"e2","value":"john@example.com"}]'
surf select e5 "Option A"
surf select e5 --by label "Display Text"
surf upload --ref e5 --files "/path/to/file.txt"

surf frame.list
surf frame.switch "FRAME_ID"
surf frame.main
surf frame.js --id "FRAME_ID" --code "return document.title"

surf dialog.info
surf dialog.accept
surf dialog.accept --text "response"
surf dialog.dismiss
```

Switch into an iframe before reading or acting on elements inside it.

## Evidence and diagnostics

```bash
surf screenshot
surf screenshot --output /tmp/shot.png
surf screenshot --selector ".card"
surf screenshot --full-page

surf console
surf console --stream --level error
surf network
surf network --stream
surf network.get --id "req-123"
surf network.body --id "req-123"
surf network.curl --id "req-123"
surf network.export

surf perf.metrics
surf perf.start
surf perf.stop
surf wait.element ".missing" --auto-capture --timeout 2000
```

`--auto-capture` saves the screenshot and console snapshot needed to debug failed waits.

## Emulation and stored browser state

```bash
surf emulate.network slow-3g
surf emulate.network reset
surf emulate.cpu 4
surf emulate.cpu 1
surf emulate.device "iPhone 14"
surf emulate.device --list
surf emulate.viewport --width 1280 --height 720
surf emulate.touch --enable
surf emulate.geo --lat 37.7749 --lon -122.4194
surf emulate.geo --clear

surf zoom
surf zoom 1.5
surf zoom 1
surf cookie.list
surf cookie.get --name "token"
surf cookie.clear
surf history --query "github" --max 20
surf bookmarks --query "docs"
surf bookmark.add --url "https://..." --title "My Bookmark"
```

After tests, restore network throttling; clear device settings; remove any location override; reset zoom.

## AI sites through Chrome

These commands rely on your logged-in Chrome profile. No API key is involved.

```bash
surf chatgpt "explain this code"
surf chatgpt "review" --with-page --model gpt-4o
surf chatgpt "analyze" --file document.pdf

surf gemini "summarize" --with-page
surf gemini "analyze" --file data.csv
surf gemini "a robot surfing" --generate-image /tmp/robot.png
surf gemini "hello" --model gemini-2.5-flash

surf perplexity "latest news" --model sonar
surf perplexity "deep dive" --mode research

surf grok "find viral AI posts" --deep-search
surf grok --validate
surf grok --validate --save-models

surf aistudio "redteam this" --with-page
surf aistudio "quick answer" --model gemini-3-flash-preview
surf aistudio.build "build a portfolio site" --output ./out
```

On failure, check login state, validate the UI, increase timeout for thinking models, then retry with a model name from validation output.

## Multi-step scripts

`surf do` runs a browser flow as one command, with automatic waits after page loads, clicks, keys, form fills, and tab switches.

```bash
surf do 'go "https://example.com" | click e5 | screenshot'
surf do 'go "https://example.com/login" | type "user@example.com" --selector "#email" | type "pass" --selector "#password" | click --selector "button[type=submit]"'
surf do 'go "https://example.test" | page.read' --dry-run
```

Named workflows live in `~/.surf/workflows/` or `./.surf/workflows/`.

```bash
surf workflow.list
surf workflow.info my-workflow
surf do my-workflow --email "user@example.com" --password "secret"
surf workflow.validate workflow.json
```

Workflow files can store step output, loop a fixed number of times, iterate over data, or stop when a condition passes.

```json
{
  "steps": [
    { "tool": "js", "args": { "code": "return [1,2,3]" }, "as": "items" },
    { "repeat": 5, "steps": [{ "tool": "click", "args": { "ref": "e5" } }] },
    { "each": "%{items}", "as": "item", "steps": [
      { "tool": "js", "args": { "code": "console.log('%{item}');" } }
    ]}
  ]
}
```

```bash
surf do my-workflow --file workflow.json --json
surf do 'go "https://example.org" | screenshot' --on-error stop --step-delay 100
surf do 'go "https://example.net" | wait.load' --no-auto-wait
```

## Common options

```bash
--tab-id <id>
--window-id <id>
--json
--auto-capture
--timeout <ms>
```

## Socket API

Send a JSON tool request to the Unix socket when another process needs direct access.

```bash
echo '{"type":"tool_request","method":"execute_tool","params":{"tool":"tab.list","args":{}},"id":"1"}' | nc -U /tmp/surf.sock
```

    generate_dek,
    is_wrapped_dek_envelope,
    unwrap_dek,
    unwrap_dek_with_keks,
    wrap_dek,
    wrap_dek_with_kek,
    wrapped_dek_key_id,

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

def _require_user_id(user_id: str) -> str:
    """Normalize user identifiers before using them in key derivation."""
    if not isinstance(user_id, str):
        raise TypeError("user_id must be a string")
    normalized_user_id = user_id.strip()
    if not normalized_user_id:
        raise ValueError("user_id must not be empty")
    return normalized_user_id


def _wrap_user_dek(dek: bytes, user_id: str) -> bytes:
    """Wrap a user DEK with the strongest configured server key source."""
    settings = get_settings()
    normalized_user_id = _require_user_id(user_id)
    key_encryption_key = settings.key_encryption_key_bytes
    if key_encryption_key:
        return wrap_dek_with_kek(
            dek,
            normalized_user_id,
            settings.key_encryption_key_id,
            key_encryption_key,
        )
    pepper = settings.encryption_pepper_bytes
    if pepper:
        return wrap_dek(dek, normalized_user_id, pepper)
    raise EncryptionNotConfiguredError("KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY or ENCRYPTION_PEPPER is required")


def _unwrap_user_dek(wrapped: bytes, user_id: str) -> bytes:
    """Unwrap a stored user DEK from either current or legacy storage."""
    settings = get_settings()
    normalized_user_id = _require_user_id(user_id)
    if is_wrapped_dek_envelope(wrapped):
        key_encryption_key = settings.key_encryption_key_bytes
        if not key_encryption_key:
            raise EncryptionNotConfiguredError(
                "KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY is required to unwrap versioned DEK envelopes"
            )
        keyring = settings.key_encryption_keyring_previous
        keyring[settings.key_encryption_key_id] = key_encryption_key
        return unwrap_dek_with_keks(wrapped, normalized_user_id, keyring)

    pepper = settings.encryption_pepper_bytes
    if not pepper:
        raise EncryptionNotConfiguredError("ENCRYPTION_PEPPER is required for legacy DEK unwrap")
    return unwrap_dek(wrapped, normalized_user_id, pepper)


def _stored_dek_needs_rewrap(wrapped: bytes) -> bool:
    """Return whether a DEK should be rewritten under the current KEK metadata."""
    settings = get_settings()
    if not settings.key_encryption_key_bytes:
        return False
    if not is_wrapped_dek_envelope(wrapped):
        return True
    return wrapped_dek_key_id(wrapped) != settings.key_encryption_key_id


def _store_wrapped_dek(user_id: str, encrypted_dek: bytes) -> None:
    """Persist a wrapped DEK for a user with a narrow update statement."""
    normalized_user_id = _require_user_id(user_id)
    if not isinstance(encrypted_dek, bytes):
        raise TypeError("encrypted_dek must be bytes")
    if not encrypted_dek:
        raise ValueError("encrypted_dek must not be empty")
    with get_control_db() as db:
        db.execute(
            "UPDATE users SET encrypted_dek = ? WHERE id = ?",
            (encrypted_dek, normalized_user_id),
        )
        db.commit()


def get_user_dek(user_id: str) -> bytes:
    """Retrieve and unwrap the user's DEK from the control DB."""
    normalized_user_id = _require_user_id(user_id)
    with get_control_db() as db:
        row = db.execute(
            "SELECT encrypted_dek FROM users WHERE id = ?",
            (normalized_user_id,),
        ).fetchone()
        if not row:
            raise KeyNotFoundError(f"User {normalized_user_id} not found")

        stored_dek = row["encrypted_dek"]
        if not stored_dek:
            # Serialize lazy creation, then recheck under the write lock.
            db.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
            row = db.execute(
                "SELECT encrypted_dek FROM users WHERE id = ?",
                (normalized_user_id,),
            ).fetchone()
            if not row:
                raise KeyNotFoundError(f"User {normalized_user_id} not found")
            stored_dek = row["encrypted_dek"]
            if not stored_dek:
                dek = generate_dek()
                encrypted_dek = _wrap_user_dek(dek, normalized_user_id)
                db.execute(
                    "UPDATE users SET encrypted_dek = ? WHERE id = ?",
                    (encrypted_dek, normalized_user_id),
                )
                db.commit()
                logger.info("Generated legacy account data-encryption key")
                return dek
            db.commit()

    dek = _unwrap_user_dek(stored_dek, normalized_user_id)
    if _stored_dek_needs_rewrap(stored_dek):
        _store_wrapped_dek(normalized_user_id, _wrap_user_dek(dek, normalized_user_id))
        logger.info("Rewrapped account data-encryption key")
    return dek


def wrap_new_user_dek(dek: bytes, user_id: str) -> bytes:
    """Wrap a freshly generated user DEK for account provisioning."""
    return _wrap_user_dek(dek, user_id)


def resolve_user_api_key(user_id: str, provider: str) -> str | None:
    """Look up and decrypt the user's stored BYOK key for a provider.

    Returns the plaintext API key, or None if no key is stored.
    """
    normalized_user_id = _require_user_id(user_id)
    if not isinstance(provider, str):
        raise TypeError("provider must be a string")
    normalized_provider = provider.strip()
    if not normalized_provider:
        raise ValueError("provider must not be empty")

    with get_control_db() as db:
        row = db.execute(
            "SELECT encrypted_key FROM api_keys WHERE user_id = ? AND provider = ? "
            "ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1",
            (normalized_user_id, normalized_provider),
        ).fetchone()

        if not row:
            return None

        dek = get_user_dek(normalized_user_id)
        key = decrypt_api_key(row["encrypted_key"], dek)

        db.execute(
            "UPDATE api_keys SET last_used_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP "
            "WHERE user_id = ? AND provider = ?",
            (normalized_user_id, normalized_provider),
        )
        db.commit()

    return key


def resolve_api_key_for_prompt(user_id: str, provider: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """Resolve which API key to use for a prompt.

    Returns (api_key, key_source). Authenticated users must provide BYOK keys.

    if byok_key:
        return byok_key, "byok"

# RepoPrompt Investigation

Use the user's request as the investigation target. Keep source files unchanged unless the user also requests a fix.

Start narrow.

Record the observed symptoms and reproduction steps. Read available logs. Note any known constraint, then create a small set of testable hypotheses. Call `repoprompt_context_builder` with `response_type: "question"`, including those facts and the likely subsystems.

Check important claims with Pi file tools and focused commands. Use Git history when timing or ownership matters. Call `repoprompt_manage_selection` only for a small addition that Context Builder missed.

Use `repoprompt_oracle_send` with the returned `chat_id` when selected files require cross-file reasoning. Revise hypotheses when facts change. Avoid repeating checks that already produced a clear result.

Stop when one root cause explains observed behavior and important alternatives have been ruled out. Report the root cause with precise file references. Explain its triggering conditions and rejected hypotheses. Identify likely fix locations. Name needed regression tests and any remaining uncertainty.

Write an investigation document only when the user requests one or repository policy requires it.

description: Applies implementation and review standards for completeness, validation, control flow, naming, comments, error handling, state, explicit options, and testing. Use before writing, modifying, refactoring, or reviewing code in any language.
---

# Coding Practices

Follow more specific repository conventions when they differ. Apply every relevant rule below.

## Completeness

Deliver complete behavior at the repository's quality bar. A release may omit features, but existing behavior must be sound. Do not leave TODOs, placeholder implementations, or temporary shortcuts. If work cannot be completed now, open an issue instead of leaving an unactionable comment.

## Assertions and Defensive Checks

Validate data at function boundaries. Use assertions for programmer errors and explicit exceptions for user or external input.

Pair checks across related paths. Validate data before writing it to a store and validate it again after reading it back. Check both what must be true and what must not be true, especially at valid-invalid boundaries.

Aim for at least two assertions or defensive checks in each behavior-bearing function. A function without checks should only wire calls together or delegate work.

## Control Flow

Use direct control flow and extract helpers before nesting becomes difficult to follow. Split compound conditions when each branch needs to be independently clear.

Consider whether an `else` should document the unhandled path. State invariants positively, such as `index < length`, rather than through negated boundary checks. Keep function bodies near 50 lines; longer functions usually contain more than one responsibility.

## Naming

Choose exact nouns and verbs that give the reader the correct mental model. Do not abbreviate names when the full term is clearer. Prefer names such as `source`, `target`, and `message_count` over `src`, `dst`, and `msg_cnt`.

Place units and qualifiers after the main noun, such as `latency_ms_max`, so related names sort together. Prefer paired names with similar length, and do not reuse one term for different meanings across subsystems.

## Comments and Documentation

Comments should explain why a choice exists so a reader can judge the tradeoff. Put a short description at the top of each test file that states the covered behavior and how the tests check it. Write comments as complete sentences; brief inline labels are acceptable.

## Error Handling

Handle every signaled error. Do not use a bare catch. Catch a broad exception only when the handler logs and re-raises, translates it into a meaningful domain error, or completely handles the failure. Trace each failure path, and make every caller deal explicitly with failures it can receive.

## Scope and State

Keep state small and local. Declare variables close to first use. Do not duplicate state that can drift from its source. Keep few variables alive at once so misuse remains easy to detect.

## Explicit Options

Spell out options at call sites when defaults affect behavior. Be explicit about encoding, timeouts, sort order, and other settings whose defaults could change or hide intent.

## Testing

The usual stack is Python backends with static HTML and JSON or YAML configuration, but repository conventions control. When adding functionality, update coupled test expectations such as tool or test counts. Run the full test suite after code changes.

name: tdd
description: Test-driven development for behavior-bearing code. Use whenever TDD Guard is active, when building features or fixing bugs, or when the user requests test-first work, red-green development, or integration tests.
---

# Test-Driven Development

Work in vertical Red → Green slices. This skill defines test quality and workflow; the Pi extension and Probity enforce source writes at tool boundaries.

Read `CONTEXT.md` when present, relevant ADRs, project instructions, and nearby tests before choosing a seam or naming behavior.

## Choose a public boundary

A public boundary is where behavior can be observed without reaching into implementation details.

When an existing public seam is obvious, state it briefly and proceed. Ask the user before writing a test only when the contract is unclear or materially different seams would produce different designs, costs, or coverage.

Tests should remain valid when internals are refactored without changing behavior.

See [tests.md](tests.md) for examples and [mocking.md](mocking.md) for boundary guidance.

## Write tests worth keeping

A good test describes caller-visible behavior through a public interface. Its expected value comes from an independent source such as a worked example or known literal. It fails when behavior is absent or wrong, survives internal restructuring, and makes one logical behavioral claim.

Private-method tests, internal call assertions, and project-owned collaborator mocks couple the suite to implementation. Expected results that repeat the implementation calculation or compare a value to itself are tautological. Write one test, learn from its result, and then choose the next case.

## Run one vertical slice

**Red:** Add one behavior-driving test and run the narrow relevant command. Confirm the failure comes from the expected assertion or behavior mismatch. Failures during test loading or setup do not establish a clean red. When infrastructure prevents the assertion from running, add only the placeholder needed to reach it.

**Green:** Add the minimum production behavior required by the observed failure. Run the narrow test again, followed by the broader relevant suite. Start the next behavior with a new red test.

Do not write all tests first and implementation later. Each cycle is a tracer bullet informed by the previous result.

## Refactoring

Refactoring is optional review work, not a mandatory step between every Red → Green slice. Refactor only while relevant tests are green. Do not introduce new behavior during refactoring.

## Guard interaction

Use Pi's `edit` and `write` tools for source changes so Probity can inspect pending content. Do not mutate source through shell redirection, in-place editors, patch commands, inline scripts, or other bypasses.

A guard block is evidence that the pending write lacks a valid TDD justification. Address the named problem. Do not weaken the test, alter expected behavior to match broken code, disable the guard, or search for another write path.

Only the user may disable enforcement with `/tdd off` or authorize a specific exception in the conversation.

# Python Practices Reference

Read this after the repository’s own instructions. If local `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `pyproject.toml`, `setup.cfg`, or existing code disagree with this file, follow the repository.

## Runtime

Run Python applications and tests from a virtual environment. Check for an existing `.env` before adding one. Put secrets in `.env`, not in source files. When a command depends on interpreter choice, file encoding, or a timeout, spell that out in the command or code.

```bash
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pytest
```

## Error boundaries

Raise errors that name the failure. Catch an exception only when the current function can recover or add useful context. Re-raise with `from error` so the original traceback stays attached. Use `with` for resource lifetimes: files, locks, temporary workspaces, sockets, database sessions.

```python
from contextlib import contextmanager
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Iterator

class DataProcessingError(Exception):
    """Raised when a data file cannot be processed."""

@contextmanager
def read_text(path: Path) -> Iterator[str]:
    try:
        yield path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    except FileNotFoundError as error:
        raise DataProcessingError(f"Missing input file: {path}") from error
```

## Types and validation

Annotate public callables. Also annotate constructors and constants exported at module scope. Use `list[str]`, `dict[str, object]`, and similar built-in generics unless the project still supports older Python. Validate data when it crosses a trust boundary such as a CLI argument, HTTP payload, environment variable, file, database row, or external service response. Use dataclasses or Pydantic when that matches nearby code.

```python
from dataclasses import dataclass

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Result:
    names: list[str]
    skipped_count: int

def extract_names(rows: list[dict[str, object]], key: str) -> Result:
    if key == "":
        raise ValueError("key must not be empty")

    names = [str(row[key]) for row in rows if key in row]
    skipped_count = len(rows) - len(names)
    return Result(names=names, skipped_count=skipped_count)
```

## Concurrency

Use `asyncio` for concurrent I/O in projects that already have async code. Keep CPU-heavy work out of the event loop. Use worker processes, a queue, or the project’s job system for that work. Threads are acceptable around blocking I/O libraries that lack async APIs. Set cancellation and timeout behavior explicitly.

```python
async def fetch_json(session: object, url: str, timeout_s: float) -> dict[str, object]:
    async with session.get(url, timeout=timeout_s) as response:
        return await response.json()
```

## Configuration

Read configuration near process startup, validate it there, then pass a settings object to code that needs it. Avoid `os.environ` reads inside business logic. Name feature flags after the behavior they control.

## Layout and names

Follow the layout already present. For a new package, prefer `src/<package_name>/` with tests under `tests/`. Put CLI entry points in `__main__.py` or a small command module. Keep business logic importable without starting the CLI. Use `snake_case.py` for Python files and `test_*.py` for tests.

## Documentation and comments

Write docstrings for public modules and classes. Add them to functions, fixtures, and test helpers when the name does not explain the purpose. State the contract: what the object does, what arguments matter, what it returns, and what it may raise. Keep comments for surprising decisions. Delete comments that repeat the code.

## Logging

Use the project’s logger setup. If none exists, create loggers with `logging.getLogger(__name__)`. Include IDs, file paths, counts, retry numbers, and other fields needed to debug the event. Do not log secrets, tokens, passwords, cookies, or raw customer data. Avoid expensive log formatting unless the message will be emitted.

```python
logger.info("Imported users", extra={"path": str(path), "count": imported_count})
```

## Tests

Use pytest when the repository already uses it. Add tests near the code you changed. Name the behavior under test and assert results visible to a caller. Mock external systems such as HTTP, queues, clocks, and databases; avoid mocks between functions in the same small module. Property tests fit parsers, serializers, validators, and numeric code.

## Performance

Measure before optimizing. Use `cProfile`, `time.perf_counter()`, database query logs, or a benchmark that matches the slow path. Cache pure work or work with clear invalidation. Stream large inputs with generators. Use NumPy, Pandas, or database-side work only when the project already depends on them and the data structure justifies it.

## Security

Validate input before using it in file paths, shell commands, SQL, templates, or network requests. Use parameterized database queries. Generate tokens with `secrets`. Hash passwords with a password-hashing library instead of raw hashes. Keep dependencies new enough to receive security fixes, and do not add a package for a trivial helper.

```python
import secrets

def generate_token() -> str:
    return secrets.token_urlsafe(32)
```

## Tooling

Run the formatter, linter, type checker, and tests that the repository defines. Common tools include Black or Ruff for formatting, Ruff or Flake8 for linting, mypy or pyright for type checking, pytest for tests, coverage for reports, and pre-commit for local hooks. Do not introduce a new toolchain unless the task requires it.

## Agent workflow

For a Python change: read repository guidance, activate or create a virtual environment, make the smallest change that solves the task, update tests, run the relevant checks, and report any failing command with the exact error that remains.

def _require_transfer_id(transfer_id: str) -> str:

    capability: str,
    claims: VerifiedRunnerCapability,

        raise TypeError("claims must be VerifiedRunnerCapability")

    with get_control_db() as database:

        database.execute(
            """

                expires_at, max_session_bytes, claimed_at

            (
                claims.transfer_id,
                claims.user_id,
                claims.runner_id,
                capability_hash,
                claims.expires_at,

def claim_runner_transfer_grant(
    transfer_id: str,
    capability: str,
    *,
    current_time: int | None = None,
) -> RunnerTransferGrant:
    """Atomically consume one exact unexpired capability hash for relay use."""
    normalized_transfer_id = _require_transfer_id(transfer_id)
    capability_hash = _capability_hash(capability)
    now = int(time.time()) if current_time is None else current_time
    if type(now) is not int or now < 0:
        raise ValueError("current_time must be a non-negative integer")

    with get_control_db() as database:
        database.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
        row = database.execute(
            """
            SELECT grant.*, runner.revoked_at, runner.runner_token_hash
            FROM runner_transfer_grants AS grant
            JOIN user_runners AS runner ON runner.id = grant.runner_id
            WHERE grant.transfer_id = ?
            """,
            (normalized_transfer_id,),
        ).fetchone()
        if row is None:
            database.rollback()
            raise RunnerRelayAuthorizationError("Runner relay grant was not found")
        if row["expires_at"] <= now:
            database.rollback()
            raise RunnerRelayAuthorizationError("Runner relay grant has expired")
        if row["claimed_at"] is not None:
            database.rollback()
            raise RunnerRelayAuthorizationError("Runner relay grant was already claimed")
        if row["revoked_at"] is not None or row["runner_token_hash"] is None:
            database.rollback()
            raise RunnerRelayAuthorizationError("Runner relay grant was revoked")
        if not secrets.compare_digest(row["capability_hash"], capability_hash):
            database.rollback()
            raise RunnerRelayAuthorizationError("Runner relay capability does not match")
        result = database.execute(
            """
            UPDATE runner_transfer_grants
            SET claimed_at = ?
            WHERE transfer_id = ? AND claimed_at IS NULL
            """,
            (now, normalized_transfer_id),
        )
        if result.rowcount != 1:
            database.rollback()
            raise RunnerRelayAuthorizationError("Runner relay grant was already claimed")
        database.commit()
    return RunnerTransferGrant(
        transfer_id=normalized_transfer_id,
        runner_id=row["runner_id"],
        expires_at=row["expires_at"],
        max_session_bytes=row["max_session_bytes"],

Root cause

Each browser poll creates a short-lived encrypted relay transfer. On teardown, both sides can independently retire it and later exchange duplicate `close` controls. The broker and runner agent remember retired IDs in a bounded 128-entry cache for five minutes.

The broker classified it as an unauthorized unknown transfer. The relay endpoint then closed the shared outbound runner WebSocket with 4400 in [`runner_relay_socket()`](/workspace/yinshi/backend/src/yinshi/api/runner_relay.py:45).

The subsequent symptoms are consequences:

1. Client relay cleanup or message handling encountered already-detached state and raised `Runner relay client is not attached`.
2. Its exception handler attempted another WebSocket close after a close frame had already been sent, producing `Cannot call send once a close message has been sent`.
3. The next capability request called `ensure_online()`. Despite fresh heartbeat data, [`_runner_is_connected()`](/workspace/yinshi/backend/src/yinshi/services/managed_runtime_manager.py:428) requires both a recent heartbeat and a currently registered relay socket.
4. With the socket gone, [`_ensure_online()`](/workspace/yinshi/backend/src/yinshi/services/managed_runtime_manager.py:372) invoked the Sprite service restart endpoint.
5. Restart recovery interrupted the still-unfinalized run. This explains contiguous streamed text but no terminal result event, `full_message`, or `turn_status`.

The 5,694-character assistant response was already delivered incrementally. Its length is incidental; the duration and polling churn exposed the 128-entry race.

1. Make valid transfer `close` controls unconditionally idempotent on both ends.

   - If no active transfer exists, treat the canonical close as a harmless no-op regardless of retired-cache membership.
   - Never allow it to affect an active transfer belonging to another runner.
   - Apply the symmetric rule to runner-agent browser `close` handling.

Last browser poll completed locally at 15:04:18.655. Runner heartbeat was accepted at 15:03:54 and Sprite active-task lease refreshed at 15:03:47. At 15:04:19 the shared outbound `/runner/relay` disconnected. Control immediately called `services/yinshi-runner/restart` at 15:04:20.164. New runner started at 15:04:20.776. Startup recovery marked run interrupted at 15:04:25. Database has assistant content but no full_message or turn_status. Runner logs contain no crash, protocol error, SQLCipher error, or reconnect warning before control restarted it. Previous runs at 14:57:56, 14:59:47, and 15:00:58 completed with 964, 193, and 596 events. Current ManagedRuntimeManager._ensure_online immediately restarts the Sprite service whenever broker relay state is absent, even with a fresh online heartbeat. Runner agent already has a reconnect loop with one-second initial backoff. A transient relay drop therefore becomes destructive because browser capability issuance races agent reconnection and restarts the process that owns the active prompt. Also unregister_runner still directly closes client WebSockets and raised `Cannot call send once a close message has been sent`; prior close helper covered only API endpoint paths. Need distinguish likely transport/protocol causes from destructive recovery policy, preserve authentication and liveness, and support durable prompt resumption after relay reconnect.</context>

The robust root cause is a control-plane recovery policy that interprets a transient, process-local relay absence as proof that the managed service must be restarted.

At 15:04:19, an ordinary relay interruption entered a destructive race:

1. The shared outbound `/runner/relay` disappeared from the broker.
2. Browser capability issuance called `ensure_online`.
3. `_ensure_online` saw no broker entry and immediately restarted `yinshi-runner`.
4. The restart killed the process owning active prompt `952845950ede4e4ab03055de53f11654`.
5. Startup recovery correctly—but irreversibly—marked the orphaned run interrupted.

The 15:03:54 accepted heartbeat and 15:03:47 Sprite task lease show that the runner process was alive immediately before the drop. Its existing reconnect loop would have retried after one second. Control restarted it roughly one second after disconnection, before reconnection could safely win.

### Evidence in the code

[`managed_runtime_manager.py`](/workspace/yinshi/backend/src/yinshi/services/managed_runtime_manager.py:372) combines heartbeat and relay connectivity into one boolean. If either is absent, it immediately calls `restart_service` at line 379. There is no reconnect grace period, active-prompt fence, provider health inspection, or distinction between “transport temporarily absent” and “process dead.”

[`runner_relay.py`](/workspace/yinshi/backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_relay.py:219) defines connectivity solely as membership in the broker’s in-memory `_runners` dictionary. A WebSocket disconnect removes that entry immediately at line 268. This state is local to one control process and is not a reliable service-health signal.

[`runner_agent.py`](/workspace/yinshi/backend/src/yinshi/runner_agent.py:922) already reconnects relay failures with a one-second initial backoff while preserving the same `RunnerWorkerManager`. That is the intended non-destructive recovery mechanism.

[`runner_worker.py`](/workspace/yinshi/backend/src/yinshi/runner_worker.py:123) marks every active prompt interrupted after process replacement. Therefore the observed interruption is expected once control forces a restart; it is not evidence that the original relay drop killed prompt execution.

The partial assistant row without `full_message` or `turn_status` is also consistent with abrupt process loss: incremental content is committed in [`stream.py`](/workspace/yinshi/backend/src/yinshi/api/stream.py:1060), while complete turn state is written only on a result or finalization at lines 1080 and 1154.

### Initiating failure versus root cause

The exact initiator of the 15:04:19 WebSocket drop remains unproven. Plausible causes include a proxy/network transient, control worker lifecycle event, ping timeout, or normal WebSocket teardown race. There is no supporting evidence for a protocol rejection, oversized frame, SQLCipher failure, authentication rejection, runner crash, or retired-transfer eviction.

That initiating transport cause should be instrumented, but it is not the robust application root cause. WebSockets can disconnect normally. The correctness defect is that one transient disconnect is allowed to terminate unrelated durable prompt work.

The `Cannot call send once a close message has been sent` exception is most likely secondary. [`unregister_runner`](/workspace/yinshi/backend/src/yinshi/services/runner_relay.py:261) directly closes attached client sockets after the runner is already disconnected. A client endpoint may already have sent its own close frame. This can obscure cleanup and telemetry, but it does not explain why the shared outbound runner socket disappeared first.

### Fix plan

1. **Remove relay absence as an immediate restart trigger.**
   When identity is valid and heartbeat is fresh, `_ensure_online` should wait for broker reconnection for a bounded grace period longer than the agent’s initial backoff. Capability issuance can wait or return a retryable “runner reconnecting” response. It must not restart the service.

2. **Separate four states explicitly.**
   Track authenticated identity, heartbeat freshness, relay attachment, and provider/process health independently. Only restart after stronger evidence such as stale heartbeat plus failed relay recovery, or an authoritative provider health check showing the service stopped.

3. **Fence restarts while prompts are active.**
   Persist an active-prompt lease or execution count outside broker memory. Any automated restart must refuse or defer while a prompt owns that lease, except for an explicit operator action or confirmed dead process.

4. **Make relay reconnection transparent to prompt execution.**
   Keep prompt execution owned by the worker/run journal rather than by one browser relay transfer. After runner relay reconnection, issue a fresh capability and let the browser resume polling the same `run_id` and sequence cursor. A lost transfer must not cancel the underlying prompt.

5. **Add durable execution attachment.**
   Persist a prompt execution identifier, owner generation, event cursor, and lease. On runner-agent or control reconnect, reattach to the existing worker/sidecar execution. On actual process restart, attempt reattachment before declaring the run interrupted. If the underlying executor cannot support reattachment, retain the active-prompt restart fence as the safety boundary.

6. **Make unrecoverable interruption internally consistent.**
   If resumption truly fails, atomically append the terminal interruption event, set `prompt_runs.status`, release the session, and finalize the partial assistant message with an explicit interrupted `turn_status` and suitable stored-turn representation. Do not leave content with both terminal fields null.

7. **Use one idempotent WebSocket close helper everywhere.**
   Apply it inside broker paths including `unregister_runner`, replacement, maintenance, rejection, and revocation—not only API endpoints. Suppress already-closed/send-after-close errors while ensuring broker maps and sender tasks are cleaned up.

8. **Add targeted regression tests.**

   - Fresh heartbeat + missing relay never calls `restart_service`.
   - Relay reconnects after one-second backoff and capability issuance succeeds.
   - An active prompt continues producing journal events across relay reconnect.
   - Concurrent browser polls share the same reconnect wait without causing a restart.
   - Stale heartbeat plus absent relay eventually permits a health-checked restart.
   - Double WebSocket close during `unregister_runner` is harmless.
   - Actual restart either reattaches the durable execution or finalizes all prompt/message state consistently.

9. **Improve observability.**
   Log WebSocket close code/reason and connection generation on both ends; record why `ensure_online` chose wait, reconnect, or restart; include heartbeat age, lease age, active-prompt count, and provider health. This should identify the transport initiator in a future recurrence without exposing capabilities or tokens.

The immediate production mitigation is to disable automatic Sprite restart when the heartbeat is fresh and let the runner’s reconnect loop win. The durable fix is to make prompts survive relay replacement and to reserve process restart for independently confirmed process failure.

async def test_concurrent_ensure_online_calls_share_one_restart(
    auth_client,
) -> None:
    """Concurrent waiters must share one manager-owned wake operation."""
    tenant = getattr(auth_client, "yinshi_tenant")
    wake_now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    runner_id, _, noise_key = _store_ready_runtime(tenant.user_id, wake_now)
    provider_started = asyncio.Event()
    release_provider = asyncio.Event()
    connected = False

    class BlockingProvider(FakeProvider):
        async def restart_service(
            self,
            name: str,
            *,
            service_name: str,
            monitor_duration: float | None,
        ) -> None:
            await super().restart_service(
                name,
                service_name=service_name,
                monitor_duration=monitor_duration,
            )
            provider_started.set()
            await release_provider.wait()

    def is_runner_connected(candidate_runner_id: str) -> bool:
        assert candidate_runner_id == runner_id
        return connected

    provider = BlockingProvider()
    manager = _manager(
        provider,
        FakeInstaller(),
        is_runner_connected=is_runner_connected,
        clock=lambda: wake_now,
    )

    first = asyncio.create_task(manager.ensure_online(tenant.user_id))
    await provider_started.wait()
    second = asyncio.create_task(manager.ensure_online(tenant.user_id))
    await asyncio.sleep(0)
    connected = True
    release_provider.set()

    first_runner, second_runner = await asyncio.gather(first, second)
    await manager.aclose()

    assert first_runner.runner_id == runner_id
    assert first_runner.runner_public_key == noise_key
    assert second_runner == first_runner
    assert [call[0] for call in provider.calls].count("restart") == 1

@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_ensure_online_accepts_reconnect_exactly_at_deadline(
    auth_client,
) -> None:
    """The final permitted sleep may establish both liveness signals."""
    tenant = getattr(auth_client, "yinshi_tenant")
    started_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    current = started_at
    runner_id, _, noise_key = _store_ready_runtime(tenant.user_id, current)
    deadline = started_at + timedelta(seconds=10)
    connected = False
    sleeps: list[float] = []

    async def sleep(seconds: float) -> None:
        nonlocal current, connected
        sleeps.append(seconds)
        current += timedelta(seconds=seconds)
        if current == deadline:
            _set_runner_heartbeat(runner_id, current)
            connected = True

    provider = FakeProvider()
    manager = _manager(
        provider,
        FakeInstaller(),
        is_runner_connected=lambda candidate_runner_id: (
            candidate_runner_id == runner_id and connected
        ),
        clock=lambda: current,
        sleep=sleep,
    )

    runner = await manager.ensure_online(tenant.user_id)
    await manager.aclose()

    assert runner.runner_id == runner_id
    assert runner.runner_public_key == noise_key
    assert current == deadline
    assert sleeps == [1.0] * 10
    assert provider.calls == []


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_ensure_online_returns_connected_runtime_without_restart(
    auth_client,
) -> None:
    """A connected managed runtime must not disrupt active relay transfers."""
    tenant = getattr(auth_client, "yinshi_tenant")
    wake_now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    runner_id, sprite_name, noise_key = _store_ready_runtime(
        tenant.user_id,
        wake_now,
    )
    provider = FakeProvider()
    connected_runner_ids: list[str] = []

    def is_runner_connected(runner_id: str) -> bool:
        connected_runner_ids.append(runner_id)
        return True

    manager = _manager(
        provider,
        FakeInstaller(),
        is_runner_connected=is_runner_connected,
        clock=lambda: wake_now,
    )

    runner = await manager.ensure_online(tenant.user_id)
    await manager.aclose()

    assert runner.runner_id == runner_id
    assert runner.runner_public_key == noise_key

This plan covers technical readiness for managed public execution. Commerce, legal pages, onboarding, and unrelated SaaS work remain deferred.

## Current state

Most high-risk platform work is complete. Each managed user receives a private Fly Sprite. FastAPI remains the browser authorization boundary. The encrypted runner relay provides outbound-only guest connectivity.

Runtime changes require exact generation, job, owner, token, and expiry values. The control plane stores durable operation state outside provider calls.

Guests encrypt backups before transfer. Independent versioned storage receives ciphertext only. Restore uses a non-active candidate and atomic activation. Failed candidates lose runner authority. Failures after activation preserve the new active runtime.

Exact-version deletion, retention, and uncertain upload reconciliation are durable. Relay maintenance survives reconnects and process restarts. SQLCipher, privacy controls, and fail-closed startup checks are implemented.

The backend passes 1,263 tests with strict static checks. Public launch remains blocked by configuration and the provisioning route.

Four launch gates remain.

## Gate 1: confirm Sprite storage encryption

Resolve this before another large implementation. Unsupported provider verification could invalidate the current storage design.

Fly documentation states that Fly Volumes use encryption at rest by default. Current public material does not clearly bind that status to Sprite storage identity.

The `.yinshi-encrypted-storage` file is not sufficient. A guest can create this file on unencrypted storage.

Ask Fly for the exact Sprite storage model, encryption guarantee, and stable storage identifier. Inspect Sprite API responses for an authoritative encryption field. Confirm whether encryption can be disabled or storage can be replaced silently.

If Fly exposes a trustworthy status, bind it to the exact Sprite or storage identifier. Recheck it during provisioning and after identity changes.

If Fly offers only an account-level contractual guarantee, compare that guarantee with the threat model. If neither option is acceptable, keep launch blocked. Use inspectable encrypted Fly Volumes or guest-managed filesystem encryption instead.

Completion condition: the project has one approved storage-encryption contract that can be enforced or audited.

## Gate 2: reconcile provider Sprites

This is the next coding task after the provider decision.

Current SQL reconciliation marks abandoned provisioning work. It does not compare provider inventory with durable runtime state. A crash can leave candidates or retired source Sprites running indefinitely.

Add bounded Sprite inventory support in `backend/src/yinshi/services/sprites.py`. Add a dedicated hosted reconciler near `managed_runtime_manager.py`. Use `managed_runners.py` and `managed_backups.py` to build the durable keep set.

The keep set must include active runtime identifiers, running-operation source identifiers, and candidate identifiers. It must also include deterministic candidate names that may predate catalog publication.

The reconciler must validate every provider page and filter by the configured Yinshi prefix. It must apply a grace interval. It must re-read durable state immediately before deletion.

Obsolete runner authority must be revoked before provider deletion when SQL still contains that identity. Provider not-found responses count as successful deletion. Uncertain failures remain retryable.

Hosted startup must finish initial reconciliation before publishing managed managers. Local Podman startup must not change.

Tests must cover active retention, abandoned provisioning, unrecorded candidates, retired sources, incomplete pagination, malformed responses, concurrent provisioning, and uncertain deletion.

Completion condition: every Yinshi-managed Sprite is retained by durable state or removed through a retryable process.

## Gate 3: cover every restore crash boundary

Guest restore journals filesystem transitions, but dedicated crash coverage exercises only one interrupted transition.

Expand `backend/tests/test_managed_restore_crash_recovery.py`. Add controlled failures around transaction creation, state-file replacement, root movement, root installation, directory synchronization, result publication, and cleanup.

Each retry must produce one coherent result. Both roots must remain old or both roots must be restored. Mixed roots are never acceptable.

Control-plane tests must also cover candidate creation before catalog publication, archive transfer, guest completion, source maintenance, activation, source deletion, and final operation completion.

Every case must check active runner identity, candidate authority, operation ownership, and cleanup results.

Completion condition: every durable restore phase resumes safely after guest or control-plane interruption.

## Gate 4: run live source-loss recovery

Use a real independent versioned bucket and private temporary Sprites. Fly checkpoints cannot serve as the recovery source.

Create representative SQLite and file data. Back it up, simulate a lost multipart completion response, then confirm one immutable object version is accepted.

Delete the source Sprite. Restore into a replacement. Check database integrity, files, sessions, runner identity separation, retention, and exact-version deletion.

Restart the control plane at selected restore phases. Confirm that no source, candidate, object version, or multipart upload remains leaked.

Record the commit, timestamps, version identifiers, integrity results, and cleanup outcome. Keep tenant paths and secrets out of logs.

Automate this drill as a scheduled staging workflow. Keep it separate from ordinary pull-request checks.

Completion condition: destructive source-loss recovery succeeds repeatedly against real provider services.

## Operational controls

Before launch, alert on stale backups, stuck operations, lease loss, restore failure, orphan reconciliation failure, storage preflight failure, and deletion failure.

Publish one recovery runbook. It must name ownership, escalation, shutdown, rollback, and cleanup steps.

## Launch decision

Enable managed public launch only after all four gates pass. Keep both current launch blocks active until the final release change.

A private managed beta can defer commerce and legal work. import asyncio,httpx

SERVICE="yinshi-verify-reconnect-log"; OUTPUT="/home/sprite/.config/yinshi/verify-reconnect-log.txt"
async def main():
 s=get_settings()
 with get_control_db() as db: sprite=db.execute("SELECT sprite_external_id FROM managed_runtimes WHERE user_id=?",("5b95936526e236f37d3a6f3a7d8876fb",)).fetchone()[0]
 token=s.sprites_api_token; assert token is not None
 async with httpx.AsyncClient(base_url=s.sprites_api_url,follow_redirects=False) as http:
  c=SpritesClient(api_token=token.get_secret_value(),http_client=http)
  try:
   await c.delete_service(sprite,service_name=SERVICE); await c.delete_file(sprite,path=OUTPUT)
   await c.configure_service(sprite,service_name=SERVICE,command="/bin/bash",args=("-lc",f"tail -n 2500 /.sprite/logs/services/yinshi-runner.log > {OUTPUT}; sleep 60"),environment={},directory="/",needs=(),monitor_duration=30)
   text=(await c.read_file(sprite,path=OUTPUT,max_bytes=3145728)).decode(errors="replace")
   lines=[line for line in text.splitlines() if line[:23] >= "2026-08-23T16:33:00.000"]
   print("\n".join(lines[-1200:]))
  finally:
   await c.delete_service(sprite,service_name=SERVICE); await c.delete_file(sprite,path=OUTPUT)
asyncio.run(main())
PY
REMOTE

return runs.run('heartbeat-transient-retry', {agent:'worker', context:'fork', task:[
'You are sole writer. Fix managed runner process exit on transient heartbeat failure. Strict red-green TDD. Do not commit, push, deploy, or touch .pi-subagents/.',
'',
'Controlled production facts:',
'- During active prompt run 9719e92d862c4df69aea5eae440dd1b1, control backend restarted.',
'- Relay reconnect policy worked, but heartbeat POST landed during downtime and returned HTTP 502.',
'- runner_agent._heartbeat_loop re-raised every non-401 HTTPStatusError.',
'- run_agent uses FIRST_COMPLETED, so heartbeat task failure cancelled relay/worker ownership and exited the process.',
'- Sprite supervisor restarted it, interrupting the active prompt.',
'',
'Required behavior:',
'1. _heartbeat_loop must retry transient network HTTPError failures, HTTP 429, and HTTP 5xx with bounded exponential backoff.',
'2. A successful heartbeat resets backoff and resumes normal heartbeat interval.',
'3. HTTP 401 remains fatal with current sanitized token-rejected error.',
'4. Other 4xx responses remain fatal with a sanitized local error.',
'5. Response validation, capability signing key mismatch, invalid body, and non-HTTP exceptions remain fail-closed.',
'6. Logs may include only safe status code or generic network category. No URL query, token, response body, user ID, or prompt data.',
'7. Keep the existing worker manager, relay task, Sprite task lease, and active prompt alive during transient heartbeat outages.',
'',
'TDD:',

---
name: rp-investigate
description: Investigate complex bugs with RepoPrompt Context Builder and targeted repository checks. Use when root cause is unclear or crosses several files.
compatibility: Requires RepoPrompt MCP and local repository tools.
---

# RepoPrompt Investigation

Use the user's request as the investigation target. Keep source files unchanged unless the user also requests a fix.

Start narrow.

Record the observed symptoms and reproduction steps. Read available logs. Note any known constraint, then create a small set of testable hypotheses. Call `repoprompt_context_builder` with `response_type: "question"`, including those facts and the likely subsystems.

Check important claims with Pi file tools and focused commands. Use Git history when timing or ownership matters. Call `repoprompt_manage_selection` only for a small addition that Context Builder missed.

Use `repoprompt_oracle_send` with the returned `chat_id` when selected files require cross-file reasoning. Revise hypotheses when facts change. Avoid repeating checks that already produced a clear result.

Stop when one root cause explains observed behavior and important alternatives have been ruled out. Report the root cause with precise file references. Explain its triggering conditions and rejected hypotheses. Identify likely fix locations. Name needed regression tests and any remaining uncertainty.

Write an investigation document only when the user requests one or repository policy requires it.

---
name: coding-practices
description: Applies implementation and review standards for completeness, validation, control flow, naming, comments, error handling, state, explicit options, and testing. Use before writing, modifying, refactoring, or reviewing code in any language.
---

# Coding Practices

Follow more specific repository conventions when they differ. Apply every relevant rule below.

## Completeness

Deliver complete behavior at the repository's quality bar. A release may omit features, but existing behavior must be sound. Do not leave TODOs, placeholder implementations, or temporary shortcuts. If work cannot be completed now, open an issue instead of leaving an unactionable comment.

## Assertions and Defensive Checks

Validate data at function boundaries. Use assertions for programmer errors and explicit exceptions for user or external input.

Pair checks across related paths. Validate data before writing it to a store and validate it again after reading it back. Check both what must be true and what must not be true, especially at valid-invalid boundaries.

Aim for at least two assertions or defensive checks in each behavior-bearing function. A function without checks should only wire calls together or delegate work.

## Control Flow

Use direct control flow and extract helpers before nesting becomes difficult to follow. Split compound conditions when each branch needs to be independently clear.

Consider whether an `else` should document the unhandled path. State invariants positively, such as `index < length`, rather than through negated boundary checks. Keep function bodies near 50 lines; longer functions usually contain more than one responsibility.

## Naming

Choose exact nouns and verbs that give the reader the correct mental model. Do not abbreviate names when the full term is clearer. Prefer names such as `source`, `target`, and `message_count` over `src`, `dst`, and `msg_cnt`.

Place units and qualifiers after the main noun, such as `latency_ms_max`, so related names sort together. Prefer paired names with similar length, and do not reuse one term for different meanings across subsystems.

## Comments and Documentation

Comments should explain why a choice exists so a reader can judge the tradeoff. Put a short description at the top of each test file that states the covered behavior and how the tests check it. Write comments as complete sentences; brief inline labels are acceptable.

## Error Handling

Handle every signaled error. Do not use a bare catch. Catch a broad exception only when the handler logs and re-raises, translates it into a meaningful domain error, or completely handles the failure. Trace each failure path, and make every caller deal explicitly with failures it can receive.

## Scope and State

Keep state small and local. Declare variables close to first use. Do not duplicate state that can drift from its source. Keep few variables alive at once so misuse remains easy to detect.

## Explicit Options

Spell out options at call sites when defaults affect behavior. Be explicit about encoding, timeouts, sort order, and other settings whose defaults could change or hide intent.

## Testing

The usual stack is Python backends with static HTML and JSON or YAML configuration, but repository conventions control. When adding functionality, update coupled test expectations such as tool or test counts. Run the full test suite after code changes.

---
name: tdd
description: Test-driven development for behavior-bearing code. Use whenever TDD Guard is active, when building features or fixing bugs, or when the user requests test-first work, red-green development, or integration tests.
---

# Test-Driven Development

Work in vertical Red → Green slices. This skill defines test quality and workflow; the Pi extension and Probity enforce source writes at tool boundaries.

Read `CONTEXT.md` when present, relevant ADRs, project instructions, and nearby tests before choosing a seam or naming behavior.

## Choose a public boundary

A public boundary is where behavior can be observed without reaching into implementation details.

When an existing public seam is obvious, state it briefly and proceed. Ask the user before writing a test only when the contract is unclear or materially different seams would produce different designs, costs, or coverage.

Tests should remain valid when internals are refactored without changing behavior.

See [tests.md](tests.md) for examples and [mocking.md](mocking.md) for boundary guidance.

## Write tests worth keeping

A good test describes caller-visible behavior through a public interface. Its expected value comes from an independent source such as a worked example or known literal. It fails when behavior is absent or wrong, survives internal restructuring, and makes one logical behavioral claim.

Private-method tests, internal call assertions, and project-owned collaborator mocks couple the suite to implementation. Expected results that repeat the implementation calculation or compare a value to itself are tautological. Write one test, learn from its result, and then choose the next case.

## Run one vertical slice

**Red:** Add one behavior-driving test and run the narrow relevant command. Confirm the failure comes from the expected assertion or behavior mismatch. Failures during test loading or setup do not establish a clean red. When infrastructure prevents the assertion from running, add only the placeholder needed to reach it.

**Green:** Add the minimum production behavior required by the observed failure. Run the narrow test again, followed by the broader relevant suite. Start the next behavior with a new red test.

Do not write all tests first and implementation later. Each cycle is a tracer bullet informed by the previous result.

## Refactoring

Refactoring is optional review work, not a mandatory step between every Red → Green slice. Refactor only while relevant tests are green. Do not introduce new behavior during refactoring.

## Guard interaction

Use Pi's `edit` and `write` tools for source changes so Probity can inspect pending content. Do not mutate source through shell redirection, in-place editors, patch commands, inline scripts, or other bypasses.

A guard block is evidence that the pending write lacks a valid TDD justification. Address the named problem. Do not weaken the test, alter expected behavior to match broken code, disable the guard, or search for another write path.

Only the user may disable enforcement with `/tdd off` or authorize a specific exception in the conversation.

Use when working in Python repositories or files such as .py, .pyi, .ipynb, pyproject.toml, requirements.txt, setup.py, setup.cfg, pytest.ini, tox.ini, Pipfile, poetry.lock, uv.lock, or when the user asks about Python, pytest, mypy, FastAPI, Django, Flask, Pydantic, packaging, virtualenv, pip, Poetry, or uv.

# Python Practices

Use this skill for any Python task, from implementation through project setup.

## Repository Conventions

Inspect repository guidance before making changes. Read local `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, project configuration, dependency files, and nearby Python code. Repository conventions take priority over this skill.

## Canonical Reference

Before changing Python code, read and apply [the Python practices reference](references/python-practices.md). Use only the sections relevant to the task. Do not impose a tool, layout, or framework that the repository does not already use.

## Environment

Use the project's virtual environment before running Python applications or installing dependencies. If none exists, create one according to repository conventions.

## Changes and Verification

When behavior changes, update tests that use the repository's existing setup. Prefer pytest only when the repository already uses it. Run the configured formatting and static-analysis checks. When the repository has no relevant configuration, follow the canonical reference.

If an established repository convention conflicts with the reference, follow the repository. Briefly report an intentional deviation when it affects the result.

---
name: pi-subagents
description: |
  Delegate work to builtin or custom subagents with single-agent, parallel,
  scripted, compatibility-chain, async, forked-context, and coordinated workflows. Use
  for advisory review, implementation handoffs, and multi-step tasks where a
  single agent should stay in control while other agents contribute context,
  planning, or execution.
---

# Pi Subagents

This skill is for the main parent orchestrator only. Do not inject or follow it inside spawned child subagents. The parent session owns delegation, orchestration, review fanout, and final fix-worker launches. Ordinary children should not run their own subagent workflows; the explicit exception is a delegated fanout child whose resolved builtin `tools` includes `subagent`, and that child may use `subagent` only for the fanout work the parent assigned.

Use this skill when the parent orchestrator needs one specialized child or composed orchestration. Use `workflowScript` for all execution, including one isolated child. Use `return runs.run("main", { agent, task })` for one child and `runs.all([...])` for coordinated waves: sequence, parallelism, branching, retries, gate monitors, and aggregation. Scripted workflows start asynchronously by default; pass `async:false` only for a small foreground run.

## How to use this router

Read the matching reference file before acting. Paths are relative to this `SKILL.md`; resolve them against `skills/pi-subagents/` and load them with the read tool.

| Task | Read |
| --- | --- |
| Decide whether to delegate, choose agents, compare tool versus slash commands, apply prompt techniques, or understand builtin roles | `references/prompting-and-roles.md` |
| Run one-child, scripted, async, scheduled, mission-backed, forked, watchdog, oracle, or intercom-coordinated workflows | `references/execution-controls.md` |
| List/create/update/delete/eject/disable agents or chains, edit agent files, use prompt-template integration, or expose extension RPC | `references/management-authoring-rpc.md` |
| Check safety constraints, best practices, standard workflows, or error handling | `references/constraints-and-recipes.md` |

For broad or uncertain requests, read more than one reference. For complex work, start with `references/prompting-and-roles.md` and `references/execution-controls.md`, then consult `references/constraints-and-recipes.md` before launching or reviewing child work.

## Always-on constraints

- Keep the parent as orchestrator and final decision-maker.
- Use one writer per cwd/worktree unless isolated worktrees are intentional.
- For cross-codebase work, record the target repo, explicit `cwd`, authority boundary, and expected output before launch. Do not assume the parent session cwd is the child repo.
- For parallel fanout, compare child prompts before launch. Do not send clone prompts with only issue numbers, titles, or broad file globs swapped; each child needs a lane-specific task, source seam, prior evidence, and decision that remains distinct without the item number. Launch that fanout as one async `workflowScript` with stable keys and aggregate output unless there is truly only one child.
- Prefer fresh-context review/validation fanout, then synthesize and apply fixes in the parent.
- Use async/background by default when work can proceed independently; do not poll just to wait. For adaptive gates, branch in `workflowScript`. Approval controls remain available only for already-running durable legacy chains.
- Preserve capability ceilings, including child tool restrictions and session-scoped allowed-agent restrictions.
- Escalate unresolved product, architecture, authority, release, merge, or safety decisions upward instead of letting a child decide silently.
- Treat receipts, CI, review bots, and external-run records as evidence, not authority to merge, close, comment, publish, or release.
- As a conservative orchestration policy, do not pass `turnBudget`, a hard `toolBudget`, or a tight `usageBudget` to mutation-capable workers. The default tool budget blocks read/search tools rather than mutation tools, and reported usage has no reservation model. If a worker is interrupted after a tool call starts, checkpoint after the current tool returns with changed files, build/test state, and commit or PR state.

Identify one root cause and exact fix locations. Do not edit.</task><context>Repository is at 6fc1664. Production facts: prompt run ef06d661e1d843e084511008ad49089f began 18:01:22. It had 565 contiguous events and 2899 assistant characters. At 18:02:05 control logged runner relay close code 1006. At 18:02:06 guest log shows a fresh runner-agent startup. Control did not call the Sprite restart endpoint. Heartbeats were successful through 18:01:53. Guest log has no Python traceback or graceful shutdown line before restart. SQLCipher printed HMAC page errors at 18:01:56, but prompt event reads continued through sequence 503 at 18:02:04. New runner startup recovery marked run interrupted at 18:02:08. Prior fixes added control reconnect waits, browser polling retries, and heartbeat retries. Inspect runner process lifecycle, Sprite service configuration, platform task leases, relay loop ownership, memory or runtime limits, and abrupt-exit paths. State which facts distinguish app exit, supervisor restart, OOM, service monitor, or platform suspension.</context>

{"backend":"headless","chat_id":"025968B3-616F-4EEC-87F4-AB874C9FDEF4","response":"The deployed runner was vulnerable to losing its Sprite keepalive lease through a cross-process task-name collision. That can cold-suspend the Sprite during an active prompt; the Sprite service manager then starts a fresh runner on wake. Control-plane reconnect-first behavior cannot preserve an in-memory prompt across that process replacement.

## Root cause

At `6fc1664`, every `SpriteTaskLease` uses the same global task:

- `backend/src/yinshi/services/sprite_task_lease.py:13-15`
  - Path: `/v1/tasks/yinshi-active`
  - Expiry: `5m`
  - Refresh: every `60s`

The runner acquires a permanent base reference in `backend/src/yinshi/runner_agent.py:1000-1016`, intended to keep the Sprite active for the runner’s entire lifetime.

However, the backup guest independently creates another `SpriteTaskLease` at `backend/src/yinshi/managed_backup_guest.py:802-803` and closes it at `:815-816`. Closing that independent object unconditionally deletes `/v1/tasks/yinshi-active` in `backend/src/yinshi/services/sprite_task_lease.py:82-93,134-146`.

Those reference counts are process-local. Therefore:

1. Runner believes it still holds `yinshi-active`.
2. Backup/maintenance process deletes that same provider-level task.
3. Until the runner’s next 60-second refresh, the Sprite has no task hold.
4. Sprite idle detection can suspend it after roughly 30 seconds.
5. A subsequent request wakes it cold, and the configured `yinshi-runner` service starts a fresh Python process.

Sprites explicitly distinguish tasks from services: tasks keep the current run active, while services are restarted on crashes and cold wakes. [Keeping a Sprite Running](https://docs.sprites.dev/keeping-sprites-running/), [Services](https://docs.sprites.dev/concepts/services/)

## Why the evidence fits

- Relay close `1006` at 18:02:05 followed by fresh startup at 18:02:06 shows the relay loss was a consequence of process/VM loss, not a recoverable WebSocket interruption.
- The runner already reconnects indefinitely on `ConnectionClosed`, `OSError`, and timeout at `runner_agent.py:1032-1051`. A network-only failure would not execute `main()` again.
- Control made no Sprite restart call, excluding `ManagedRuntimeManager`’s explicit restart path at `backend/src/yinshi/services/managed_runtime_manager.py:413-419`.
- Successful heartbeats through 18:01:53 establish that the old process was alive shortly before the loss. They do not keep a Sprite active: they are outbound requests.
- No traceback or graceful-shutdown line favors an external freeze/kill over an ordinary uncaught Python exception.
- Recovery marking the run interrupted at 18:02:08 confirms the prompt journal was reopened by a new worker process.
- SQLCipher HMAC errors are not the immediate trigger: prompt reads continued through sequence 503 at 18:02:04.
- The 565 events and 2,899 assistant characters are not intrinsically large enough to establish OOM.

## Exact fixes

Primary fix locations:

- `backend/src/yinshi/services/sprite_task_lease.py:13,26-56,119-146`
  - Remove the module-global task identity.
  - Require an owner-specific validated task name/path in the constructor.
  - Ensure each lease refreshes and deletes only its own task.

- `backend/src/yinshi/runner_agent.py:1000`
  - Construct a runner-owned lease, such as `yinshi-runner`, whose lifetime is the runner process.

- `backend/src/yinshi/managed_backup_guest.py:802`
  - Construct a job-owned lease, such as `yinshi-backup-<job_id>`, so backup cleanup cannot delete the runner hold.

- `backend/tests/test_runner_agent_managed.py` and the Sprite-task-lease tests
  - Add a regression test with two independent leases proving closing the backup lease leaves the runner task intact.

Useful diagnostic hardening:

- `backend/src/yinshi/services/sprites.py:297-305,445-470`
  - Preserve provider `restart_count` and any exit/signal fields rather than parsing only PID, start time, status, and error.
- Add task-name/upsert/delete and expiry logging in `sprite_task_lease.py` without credentials.

## Alternative classifications

| Mechanism | What the facts say |
|---|---|
| Ordinary app exit | Less likely: an uncaught Python exception should normally produce a traceback. |
| Sprite service supervisor | It performed the fresh startup, but is the restart mechanism, not the initiating cause. |
| OOM/SIGKILL | Still observationally possible because abrupt OOM produces no Python traceback. It requires provider/cgroup OOM evidence or service exit metadata; current code records neither. No per-service memory limit appears in the service definition. |
| Service monitor duration | Excluded. `monitor_duration` only controls how long the configure/start API streams startup logs; it is not a watchdog or runtime limit. The runner uses `None` at `managed_guest_installer.py:265-274`. |
| Platform suspension | Best fit. A warm wake preserves the process, whereas a cold wake starts services afresh. The shared task deletion supplies the missing reason suspension was possible during an active prompt. |

No files were edited."}

class SpriteTaskLeaseError(RuntimeError):

class SpriteTaskLease:
    """Keep one bounded Sprite task alive while relay transfers exist."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        transport: httpx.AsyncBaseTransport | None = None,
        sleep: Sleep = asyncio.sleep,
        request_timeout_seconds: float = _DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
    ) -> None:
        if not callable(sleep):
            raise TypeError("sleep must be callable")
        if (
            isinstance(request_timeout_seconds, bool)
            or not isinstance(request_timeout_seconds, (int, float))
            or request_timeout_seconds <= 0
        ):
            raise ValueError("request_timeout_seconds must be positive")
        if transport is None:
            transport = httpx.AsyncHTTPTransport(uds=_SPRITE_API_SOCKET)
        self._client = httpx.AsyncClient(
            base_url="http://sprite",
            transport=transport,
            follow_redirects=False,
        )
        self._sleep = sleep
        self._request_timeout_seconds = float(request_timeout_seconds)
        self._lock = asyncio.Lock()
        self._references = 0
        self._refresh_task: asyncio.Task[None] | None = None
        self._closed = False

    async def acquire(self) -> None:
        """Acquire one reference and create the local task when needed."""
        async with self._lock:
            if self._closed:
                raise RuntimeError("Sprite task lease is closed")
            if self._references == 0:
                await self._put_task()
                self._refresh_task = asyncio.create_task(
                    self._refresh_loop(),
                    name="sprite-task-lease-refresh",
                )
            self._references += 1

    async def release(self) -> None:
        """Release one reference and delete the task after the final reference."""
        async with self._lock:
            if self._references == 0:
                raise RuntimeError("Sprite task lease has no references")
            self._references -= 1
            if self._references != 0:
                return
            await self._stop_refresh()
            await self._delete_task()

    async def aclose(self) -> None:
        """Delete any held task and close the local HTTP client."""
        async with self._lock:
            if self._closed:
                return
            self._closed = True
            had_references = self._references > 0
            self._references = 0
            await self._stop_refresh()
            if had_references:
                await self._delete_task()
        await self._client.aclose()

    async def _refresh_loop(self) -> None:
        """Refresh the task expiry once per minute while references remain."""
        while True:
            await self._sleep(_REFRESH_INTERVAL_SECONDS)
            async with self._lock:
                if self._references == 0 or self._closed:
                    return
                try:
                    await self._put_task()
                except SpriteTaskLeaseError:
                    logger.warning("Could not refresh managed Sprite task lease")

    async def _stop_refresh(self) -> None:
        """Stop and join the current refresh task."""
        refresh_task = self._refresh_task
        self._refresh_task = None
        if refresh_task is None or refresh_task is asyncio.current_task():
            return
        refresh_task.cancel()
        try:
            await refresh_task
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            pass

    async def _put_task(self) -> None:
        """Create or refresh the fixed local task without exposing HTTP errors."""
        failed = False
        try:
            response = await self._client.put(
                _TASK_PATH,
                json=_TASK_PAYLOAD,
                timeout=self._request_timeout_seconds,
            )
            failed = not 200 <= response.status_code < 300
        except (httpx.RequestError, TimeoutError):
            failed = True
        if failed:
            raise SpriteTaskLeaseError("Could not acquire managed Sprite task lease")

    async def _delete_task(self) -> None:
        """Best-effort delete the task while retaining expiry as crash fallback."""
        failed = False
        try:
            response = await self._client.delete(
                _TASK_PATH,
                timeout=self._request_timeout_seconds,
            )

    """Run heartbeats and outbound encrypted relay until either fails."""

            _runner_relay_loop(config, runner_token, client),
            name="runner-relay",

        tasks = (heartbeat_task, relay_task)
        try:
            done, pending = await asyncio.wait(
                tasks,
                return_when=asyncio.FIRST_COMPLETED,
            )
            for task in pending:
                task.cancel()
            await asyncio.gather(*pending, return_exceptions=True)
            for task in tasks:
                if task in done:
                    task.result()
        finally:
            for task in tasks:
                if not task.done():
                    task.cancel()
            await asyncio.gather(*tasks, return_exceptions=True)

    *,
    job_id: str,

) -> None:

    if _JOB_ID_PATTERN.fullmatch(job_id) is None:
        raise ValueError("job_id must be a canonical lowercase UUID")
    if maintenance_root.is_symlink() or not maintenance_root.is_dir():
